Governments and relevant stakeholders should actively work towards the implementation and enforcement of anti-discrimination and protective laws that are grounded in human rights standards. These measures aim to eliminate stigma, discrimination, and violence against underserved and marginalized populations. 2. Transgender and gender-diverse individuals who self-administer gender-affirming hormones must have access to evidence-based information, high-quality hormone products, and sterile injection equipment to ensure safe and effective self-care practices. 3. Digital health interventions provide valuable opportunities to promote self-care by offering information, resources, and discussion forums that empower individuals to take charge of their health. 4. Telemedicine services that facilitate client-to-provider communication can be offered as a complementary approach to traditional face-to-face healthcare services, supporting self-care interventions and improving accessibility. 5. Health workers can use targeted digital communication to educate clients about self-care interventions. This approach can help implement, monitor, and evaluate health outcomes effectively. 6. Safe and secure disposal of waste generated from self-care products should be promoted at all levels to minimize environmental impact and ensure public health safety. 7. Countries, donors, and stakeholders should prioritize environmentally sustainable procurement of self-care products. This includes selecting supplies that generate less waste, are recyclable, or produce less hazardous byproducts, as well as minimizing the quantities used. 8. A dynamic, user-friendly online platform is available to provide continuous updates on new evidence and information related to self-care interventions. This living guideline approach ensures that recommendations remain current and relevant. 9. Self-care interventions represent a promising and innovative approach to improving health and well-being. They empower individuals by increasing autonomy, choice, and accessibility, particularly in underserved populations and during global health emergencies like the COVID-19 pandemic. 10. Evidence-based normative guidance is essential to ensure that self-care interventions are of high quality and provide individuals with the tools to make informed decisions about their health and healthcare. 11. Self-care interventions can address the global shortage of healthcare workers and the increasing demand for health services, particularly in resource-limited settings. They offer a critical pathway to achieving universal health coverage (UHC) and reducing health disparities. 12. Self-care interventions align with global health initiatives, such as the WHO's Thirteenth General Programme of Work and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). They contribute to advancing primary healthcare, promoting health equity, and addressing broader determinants of health. 13. The WHO recommends self-care interventions as a vital component of achieving UHC, promoting health, and serving vulnerable populations. These interventions can improve health outcomes, increase access to services, and reduce healthcare costs. 14. Self-care interventions are particularly relevant in humanitarian crises, where health systems are often overstretched. They enable individuals and communities to manage their health effectively, even in challenging circumstances. 15. During pandemics, self-care measures such as physical distancing, mask-wearing, and hand hygiene have proven to be essential components of the global response, demonstrating the importance of empowering individuals with self-care tools. 16. Self-care interventions encompass a wide range of practices, including health promotion, disease prevention, self-medication, and rehabilitation. They can be implemented with or without the direct supervision of healthcare professionals. 17. The WHO's living guideline approach ensures that self-care recommendations are continuously updated based on new evidence, allowing for the inclusion of additional health domains and interventions over time. 18. Self-care interventions support a continuum of care and a people-centered approach to health. They empower individuals and caregivers to make choices that align with their values, lifestyles, and health needs. 19. The WHO emphasizes the importance of group education, user-friendly online information, and evidence-based tools to support the effective implementation of self-care interventions. 20. Self-care interventions are reshaping the way healthcare is perceived and accessed, offering innovative solutions to improve health outcomes and promote well-being globally.
